title: How bridges stay up
examples: What is the difference between a beam and an arch?
Which type of bridge is best for a very wide river?
How do bridges handle pulling and pushing forces?

explain.say: A beam is a simple straight structure that spans a gap.

draw.text: Beam: Straight support across a gap

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a truss bridge. Look at the top chord, the bottom chord and the triangle. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
An arch is curved and pushes the weight down and out.
Suspension bridges use strong cables hanging between towers.
Tension is the pulling force that tries to stretch things apart.
Compression is the pushing force that tries to squeeze things together.
A real bridge uses both tension and compression forces together.

faq.a: No, not all bridges use cables. Beams and arches can support weight without them. It is a good question.
asks: What if I don't use cables?
Are cables only for suspension bridges?

faq.q: What is the difference between tension and compression?
faq.a: Tension is when something pulls apart, like stretching a rubber band. Compression is when something pushes together, like squeezing a box.
asks: Can you show me pulling vs pushing?
What force pulls the bridge apart?

faq.q: Which force is strongest in an arch?
faq.a: In an arch, the main force pushing through it is compression. The shape helps keep the forces balanced.
asks: Does an arch handle pulling forces?
What force does the curve manage?

faq.q: Are suspension bridges always the biggest?
faq.a: Suspension bridges are good for long spans because the cables handle the pulling force well. But other types exist too.
asks: Are they always the longest bridges?

faq.q: Can a beam support a very wide gap?
faq.a: It is very hard for a simple beam to span a very wide gap. It needs support underneath it to prevent bending too much.
asks: How far can a beam go?
What happens if a beam is too long?

facts: Beams are best for shorter spans where support is available.
Arches convert downward force into outward horizontal thrust.
Suspension bridges use main cables to carry the roadway.
Tension forces pull materials apart, while compression forces push them together.

quiz.say: If a bridge is built using curved stone pieces, it is most likely using which structure?
quiz.why: The curved shape of an arch is designed to manage weight by pushing forces out evenly.

wrong.0: Suspension bridges rely on hanging cables, not the inherent curve of the stone structure.
wrong.1: Tension is a force, not a structural shape used to build the bridge.
wrong.3: A beam is straight, and while it can span gaps, it does not use the curved force transfer.

quiz.say: The main cables hanging between tall towers are the defining feature of which bridge type?
quiz.why: Suspension bridges are defined by their use of strong cables hanging from high towers.

wrong.0: Compression is a force, not the name of the bridge type itself.
wrong.2: Beams are simple straight supports and do not require large hanging cables.
wrong.3: Arches use compression through a curve, not hanging cables for support.

quiz.say: When a bridge supports a heavy load, the parts being squeezed together are experiencing:
quiz.why: Squeezing or being pushed together is the definition of compression force in materials.

wrong.1: Tension is the force that pulls things apart, like stretching a rope.
wrong.2: Beam is a shape, not a type of force experienced by the structure.
wrong.3: Suspension is a bridge type, not the name of the force being applied.
